The market swings underscored the fragility of diplomatic efforts to defuse tensions between Washington and Tehran amid a significant U.S. military buildup in the Middle East.

items.title: Heavy snowfall cancels training as 2026 Winter Olympics open

featured_image.name: Heavy snowfall prompts cancellation of women’s downhill training at Milan Cortina Olympics

items.description:
As the Milan-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics prepare for their February 6 opening ceremony, organizers face a climate change paradox: decades of warming have left venues dependent on artificial snow, yet an intense last-minute snowfall has now forced the cancellation of training runs.

The 2026 Games are taking place in a much warmer climate than when Cortina d'Ampezzo last hosted in 1956, highlighting the growing challenge of staging winter sports in an era of rising global temperatures.

items.title: Coronal mass ejection reaches Earth, triggering minor storm watch

featured_image.name: Powerful geomagnetic storm sparks stunning northern lights ...

items.description:
A volatile sunspot region has erupted with dozens of powerful solar flares this week, causing radio blackouts across parts of the globe and sending charged particles hurtling toward Earth that could produce visible auroras in the coming days.

The culprit is sunspot region AR4366, which emerged on January 30 and has since grown into what scientists describe as a "solar flare factory," now spanning more than 15 Earth-widths across the sun's surface. Since February 1, the region has unleashed at least 64 solar flares, including five in the X-class—the most intense category—and more than 38 medium-sized M-class events.[1][2][3][4]

The strongest eruption, an X8.1 flare that peaked at 11:57 p.m. UTC on February 1, was among the most powerful recorded during the current solar cycle. That blast triggered strong R3-level radio blackouts across the South Pacific, disrupting shortwave communications in eastern Australia and New Zealand, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center.[5][6][7][8][9][10]

items.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke by phone on Wednesday in what Trump described as an "excellent" and "thorough" conversation, their first direct communication since late November. The wide-ranging call addressed trade, Taiwan arms sales, the Iran situation, and the Russia-Ukraine war as the two leaders prepare for Trump's planned visit to Beijing in April.

items.title: US, EU, Japan forge critical minerals partnership to counter China

featured_image.name: EU's von der Leyen eyes rare-earth mining with Japan ...

items.description:
The United States, European Union, and Japan announced a strategic partnership on Wednesday to bolster critical minerals supply chain security, marking a significant expansion of Western efforts to reduce dependence on Chinese-controlled materials vital to defense, technology, and clean energy industries.

The announcement came during the inaugural Critical Minerals Ministerial in Washington, which brought together delegations from over 50 countries. Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted the summit, while Vice President JD Vance delivered opening remarks calling for a "preferential trade zone" protected by enforceable price floors.[1][2][3]

items.title: US-Iran nuclear talks back on after Arab leaders lobby Trump

featured_image.name: U.S.-Iran nuclear talks back on after Arab leaders lobby ...

items.description:
Scheduled nuclear negotiations between the United States and Iran appeared on the verge of collapse Wednesday before urgent appeals from at least nine Middle Eastern nations convinced the Trump administration to proceed with talks in Oman on Friday.

The diplomatic whiplash came after Iran demanded changes to both the venue and format of the meeting, initially planned for Istanbul. Tehran requested the talks be moved to Muscat and narrowed to a strictly bilateral format focused exclusively on nuclear issues, excluding discussions of ballistic missiles and regional proxy networks that Washington had sought to include.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil prices surge as U.S.-Iran nuclear talks collapse

featured_image.name: Oil prices edge up after US shoots down Iranian drone ... - CNBC

items.description:
Oil prices jumped more than 3% on Wednesday after reports emerged that planned nuclear talks between the United States and Iran have collapsed, reigniting fears of military conflict in the Middle East and potential disruptions to global oil supplies.

U.S. crude oil rose roughly 3.5% while global benchmark Brent climbed about 3.4% in afternoon trading, according to Investing.com. The sharp gains came after Axios reported that negotiations scheduled for Friday had been effectively canceled following a dispute over the location and scope of the discussions.[1][2][3]

items.description: Turkey and Saudi Arabia announced a sweeping expansion of economic and energy cooperation on Tuesday following Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's official visit to Riyadh, where he met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman at Al-Yamamah Palace. The two countries issued a joint statement pledging to raise bilateral trade from its current level of more than $8.6 billion to $10 billion in the short term and $30 billion over the long term, while signing agreements to develop renewable energy projects and strengthen defense ties.[1][2][3]

items.title: Study finds over 2,500 non-native plants could survive in Arctic

featured_image.name: New paper on potential new alien plants across the Arctic ...

items.description:
A new study has identified more than 2,500 plant species that could potentially survive and establish themselves in the Arctic today, raising alarm about a looming ecological threat to one of Earth's most vulnerable ecosystems.

The research, published in the journal NeoBiota, found that 2,554 alien vascular plant species could find a suitable climatic niche in the Arctic tundra if transported there, with northern Norway emerging as a primary hotspot for potential invasions.[1][2][3]
